title: Committee of  Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of  Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Regional hubs and connectivity investment
sections.summary: Regional hubs connect the island to the world, so investment in physical connectivity like Changi T5 and Tuas Port should continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: These regional hubs have helped better connect and plug our tiny island to the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: We should continue to invest and upgrade our physical connectivity, such as the building of Changi Airport Terminal 5 (T5), Tuas Port and the other infrastructure, to stay ahead of the pack.

sections.label: Budget schemes and DRC tightening
sections.summary: Existing schemes were enhanced and new ones announced, with the service sector Dependency Ratio Ceiling tightened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: Besides the enhancement and extension of the existing schemes, such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG), Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS), the Finance Minister also announced new schemes, such as Scale-up SG, Innovation Agents Programme and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: One of the highlights of this year's Budget Statement is the tightening of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) for the service sector.

sections.label: LEAD programme support for TACs
sections.summary: TACs need support, and the LEAD programme administered by Enterprise Singapore can help them drive capability development and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: So, the TACs need more support and encouragement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: I understand that there are schemes, such as the Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) programmes administered by Enterprise Singapore (ESG), that can help TACs to play a more proactive role to drive capability development and internationalisation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah
sentences.text: Can I ask what is the take-up rate so far of the LEAD programme by the TACs, and has it been effective?

sections.label: 2018 GDP growth and SME pessimism
sections.summary: 2018 GDP growth of 3.2% was lower than 2017 and achieved through declining quarters, with SME surveys showing pessimism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, though we achieved 3.2% gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 2018, which was actually lower than 2017 at 3.9%, there is a concern that we have achieved the 2018 growth through a declining quarter-to-quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Based on the feedback and survey of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) by the different chambers of commerce, there is some pessimism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But with a forecast of 1.5% to 3.5% for growth this year, this range is only of moderate growth.

sections.label: ASEAN Economic Committee 2025 plan
sections.summary: The ASEAN Economic Committee 2025 plan is underway, and ASEAN is poised to be the fourth largest economy by GDP in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Economic Committee 2025 plan is well underway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And ASEAN is poised to be the fourth largest economy by GDP in 2030 as the other countries in ASEAN hit their stride in terms of economic growth.

sections.label: Belt and Road Initiative business opportunities
sections.summary: Given uncertainty from the US-China trade conflict, the Ministry was asked how it helped businesses seize BRI opportunities since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, given that businesses face greater uncertainty and a weaker economic outlook in part due to the geopolitical uncertainty with the United States (US)-China trade conflict, is the Ministry able to share information on how it has helped our businesses seize opportunities presented by the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) since it was first announced by China in 2013?

sections.label: Regional growth and competitiveness
sections.summary: Healthy regional economic growth is to be celebrated, but Singapore must do more to stay competitive and relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Healthy economic growth in the region is to be celebrated, but this means that we will have to do more to stay competitive and relevant.

sections.label: Global-Asia node positioning
sections.summary: The Finance Minister spoke about positioning Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister spoke about positioning Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: McKinsey leading AI prediction
sections.summary: McKinsey predicts that leading AI countries could capture an additional 20% to 25% in net economic benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: McKinsey predicts that “Leading AI” countries could capture an additional 20% to 25% in net economic benefits.

sections.label: MTI plans and FTAs
sections.summary: Questions ask MTI to share plans on ports, airports, logistics, customs, data connectivity, non-physical connectivity, the Global Innovation Alliance, the Global Ready Talent Programme and ESG programmes, noting 24 FTAs with 36 partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, can MTI share our plans, moving forward to strengthen our ports, airports, logistics and customs clearance as well as data connectivity?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MTI also share how we are building up our non-physical connectivity for Asia and ASEAN?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, can MTI provide an update on how we have strengthened our footprint in Asia through the Global Innovation Alliance, share details of the upcoming Global Ready Talent Programme and provide an update on how we can help our companies internationalise through various ESG programmes?

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Teo Ser Luck, you can take both your cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We have 24 Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and Economic Partnership Agreements with 36 partners, including the recent European Union (EU)-Singapore FTA (EUSFTA).

sections.label: FTA impact indicators
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry has quantifiable indicators measuring the impact of the different FTAs, such as the number of companies benefiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have any quantifiable indicators that measure the impact of these different FTAs, for example, the number of companies benefiting from it?

sections.label: ITM awareness and business help
sections.summary: All 23 ITMs covering 80% of the Singapore economy have been launched since March 2018, but awareness of ITM specifics is still lacking and businesses need help with technology and new business models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, all 23 ITMs covering 80% of the Singapore economy have been launched since March 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Within our 10 industry groups, we hold regular dialogues and focus roadmap sessions without members having to provide resources and support from the transformation journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: However, almost a year on from the launch of the ITMS, from conversations with the broader SMF member base, it is apparent that awareness on the specifics of the ITMs is still lacking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Businesses also need help to cope with rapid changes in technology and new business models.

sections.label: Electric vehicle adoption numbers
sections.summary: Of 615,000 cars, 28,000 are electric or hybrids; of 20,000 taxis, 104 are electric; of 137,000 motorbikes, two are fully electric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of the 615,000 cars on our roads, only 28,000 are electric or hybrids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of 20,000 taxis, just 104 are electric; of 137,000 motorbikes, only two are fully electric/battery-powered.

sections.label: EV charging point targets
sections.summary: SP Group announced 1,000 charging points by 2020, while the Government stated a goal of 2,000 points in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In October 2018, SP Group announced they will be speeding up the installation of electric vehicle charging points and roll out 1,000 such points by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But in Parliament in 2016, the Government stated a goal of 2,000 charging points.

sections.label: Agri-tech startup investments
sections.summary: ESG's Seeds Capital has invested more than $90 million in early-stage tech startups with food and agri-tech solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We can use our investment and innovation infrastructure and regional hub status to boost efficiency, profitability and yield.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I understand that ESG, through its investment arm, Seeds Capital, has channeled more than $90 million worth of investments into early-stage tech startups with food and agri-tech solutions.

sections.label: Funding tailored to large local enterprises
sections.summary: It proposes tailoring funding and schemes to large local enterprises, including a special quota to hire foreign expertise with knowledge transfer.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, to tailor the funding and schemes to assist large local enterprises, as opposed to the current grants provision that is uniformly applied across all SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: For example, if the company is currently lacking in certain functional domains and the skilled expertise has to be sought from foreign talent pool in the interim, allow them to have a special quota to hire the expertise for a defined period and put in place measures that can ensure that knowledge transfer must take place to develop future inhouse expertise and the local workforce gets an opportunity to step up.

sections.label: Panel for internationalising firms
sections.summary: It proposes a panel of industry experts, executives, consultants and business owners to mentor firms seeking to internationalise.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, create a panel of expertise that can act as consultants or mentors to startups or existing firms that wish to internationalise.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, there exists a gap for these companies that are trying to navigate the business culture differences to understand which functions within their entire operations of specific industry will be more effectively performed overseas and how they can collaborate with other Singapore companies in the global arena.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, I suggest we begin with the provision of a panel made up of experts from specific industries, retired or existing senior management executives from MNCs, consultants and business owners who wish to volunteer their insights or even take a stake in the companies to enable their leap towards internationalisation.

sections.label: Overseas offices sharing tender information
sections.summary: It asks whether overseas economic offices could obtain commercial tender information to share among Singapore companies in industry cooperation circles for a small fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Would the Government consider using overseas economic offices to obtain information about commercial tenders, to be shared among relevant Singapore companies in specific industry cooperation circles, with the member firms perhaps paying a small fee to receive these alerts?

sections.label: RIE2020 enterprise and technology transfer
sections.summary: RIE2020 focuses on value creation and public-private research collaboration, but Government institutions lack technology transfer offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE2020) Plan recognises that Singapore needs to focus more on the "enterprise" component as our research and innovation base has firmed up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the four major thrusts is a sharper focus on value creation, allocating more of the R&D budget towards public-private research collaborations and helping companies to absorb new technologies to further our Future Economy and Smart Nation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While our universities and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research research institutes have offices of technology transfer to support the commercialisation of research and innovation and enhance collaboration with companies, our Government institutions do not have such setups.

sections.label: Defence technology commercialisation
sections.summary: Technology transfers have occurred, such as thermal scanners for SARS, but defence technologies have not been systematically commercialised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There has been some interesting reverse flow of technology transfers though, for example, the production of mass thermal scanners to combat the 2003 Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But there has not been a systematic push to commercialise our defence technologies, even though one in 12 scientists and engineers in Singapore is employed by the defence sector.

sections.label: Technology transfer ecosystem and ESG
sections.summary: A technology transfer ecosystem could bring together defence bodies and SMEs, and ESG provides focused Government support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One way to do this is to build a strong technology transfer ecosystem bringing together the Ministry of Defence, DSTA, DSO, ST Engineering and our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Teo Ser Luck, you can take your three cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Also, with the merging of International Enterprise (IE) Singapore and the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore to form ESG, there is additional support and very focused effort through direct Government help to support these companies.

sections.label: Dependence on MNCs and local suppliers
sections.summary: Singapore has depended on MNCs, while local companies are mainly suppliers without their own IP or branding to scale overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: For many years, we have depended on the MNCs that are in Singapore and we form a large scale of local companies which are mainly suppliers who have not developed their own IP or their own branding that can scale them up for going overseas.

sections.label: Plans to strengthen companies
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry's plans are to strengthen companies and foster their partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans moving forward to strengthen the companies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans and initiatives moving forward to foster the partnership of these companies?

sections.label: Beauty and slimming complaints
sections.summary: Residents face repossession problems, and CASE received 1,917 complaints in 2018 against beauty and slimming businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We have seen many of these through our residents when we meet them during the Meet-the-People Sessions when they come forward after having encountered problems with all their purchases – whatever they have bought, have to be repossessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: So, can the Government share if there are any regulations to tighten this, so that retailers may not over-extend their credit and consumers will not run into a risk?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In 2018, CASE received 1,917 complaints against businesses in the beauty and slimming industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This makes the industry with the highest number of complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Of these, 1,829 are in relation to the beauty industry and 88 are in relation to the slimming industry.

sections.label: Cooling-off period beauty slimming contracts
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to consider a mandatory cooling-off period for contracts with beauty and slimming businesses, to signal that unfair practices should not be used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This will send a right signal to genuine businesses that they should not use unfair business practices to persuade their customers to sign up for a package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Ministry to consider implementing a mandatory cooling-off period for contracts entered into with businesses in the beauty and slimming industries.

sections.label: Charge-back scheme awareness
sections.summary: CASE urges MAS to work with ABS and credit card issuing banks to raise awareness of charge-back schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: CASE urges the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to work with the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) and the credit card issuing banks to raise awareness of charge-back schemes with their credit card banks.

sections.label: Red Dot Power exit, Town Councils
sections.summary: EMA told Town Councils that Red Dot Power would exit the market, accounts would transfer to SP Group, and early termination fees would not apply, with the higher wholesale SP tariff applied in the interim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This consideration is also relevant for Town Councils as such statutory organisations have also benefited from the liberalisation of the electricity market earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, on 2 January this year, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) shared with Town Councils that one player, Red Dot Power, which coincidentally was in an existing electricity supply contract with the Aljunied-Hougang Town Council, would be exiting the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EMA informed the Town Council the retailer would cease to be able to purchase electricity from 4 January, and all accounts under the Town Council's purview would be transferred to the SP Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EMA also informed the Town Council that any early termination fees/charges contractually that the Town Council would have had with the affected retailer would not be applicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the interim, the wholesale SP tariff rate applied which was significantly higher than the contracted rate, at the cost of savings to the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With individual households now able to buy electricity directly from retailers, how will EMA deal with retailers that unilaterally terminate their contracts in the retail space?

sections.label: Rules, over-regulation and compliance costs
sections.summary: Some rules are needed for safety and public interest, but over-regulation could lead to high regulatory and compliance costs and delays in licence processing and business opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Some rules are needed to ensure safety, while others are needed to protect public interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But over-regulation could lead to high regulatory and compliance costs, and unnecessary delays in the processing of licence applications and maximising of business opportunities.

sections.label: Up-to-date regulations and sandboxes
sections.summary: The speaker asks how regulations are kept up-to-date without adding compliance costs, whether there will be more sandboxes, and what strategy prevents regulations from encumbering enterprise growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: How does it ensure that our regulations are kept up-to-date and do not add unnecessary compliance costs for our businesses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Will there be more sandboxes to allow and promote new business models?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: What is our strategy to ensure that the Government regulations do not encumber the growth of enterprises?

sections.label: Expiry dates for new regulations
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would consider applying expiry dates or sunset clauses to newly introduced regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider applying expiry dates or sunset clauses to newly introduced regulations?

sections.label: Four economic strategy thrusts
sections.summary: The passage lists four thrusts: deepening market linkages, transforming industries, strengthening enterprise and worker capabilities, and empowering businesses and consumers through agile regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, to deepen and diversify linkages to markets; second, to transform industries to seize new opportunities; third, to strengthen capabilities of enterprises and workers; and, fourth, to empower businesses and consumers through more agile regulations and a more pro-business environment.

sections.label: ASEAN Single Window in place
sections.summary: The ASEAN Single Window is now in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Single Window is now in place.

sections.label: ASEAN and China trade agreements
sections.summary: ASEAN agreements on e-commerce, services and investment, and the upgraded China-Singapore FTA, will boost digital connectivity, market access and investment protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Agreement on E-commerce, ASEAN Trade in Services Agreement and enhancements to the ASEAN Comprehensive Investment Agreement will boost digital connectivity, improve market access in ASEAN's growing services sector and reduce investment impediments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: With China, the upgraded China-Singapore FTA will provide businesses with enhanced investment protection, greater access to China's legal, maritime and construction services sectors, and improved Rules of Origin for petrochemical and plastics exports.

sections.label: EUSFTA European Parliament consent
sections.summary: A few weeks ago, the EUSFTA and Investment Protection Agreement received the European Parliament's consent with a clear majority.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A few weeks ago, the EUSFTA and Investment Protection Agreement received the European Parliament’s consent with a clear majority.

sections.label: Trade with FTA partners
sections.summary: Trade with FTA partners is 92% of total trade, companies saved about $730 million in tariffs in 2016, and about 1,800 companies yearly benefit from ESG efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore’s trade with our FTA partners accounts for 92% of our total trade in goods and services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our companies enjoyed tariff savings of about $730 million in 2016, a substantial increase from the $450 million enjoyed a decade prior.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since 2016, about 1,800 companies have benefited each year from ESG's efforts to build awareness of our network of trade agreements and its benefits.

sections.label: Multimodal economic link benefits
sections.summary: This multimodal and multifaceted economic link cuts transport time between the two regions from three weeks to one and lowers business costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Besides reducing the time needed to transport goods between the two regions from three weeks to one, this multimodal and multifaceted economic link will improve modern dimensions of connectivity and lower costs for businesses.

sections.label: Supporting companies overseas
sections.summary: Companies are supported through capability development, market access, manpower and financing, with overseas centres supporting over 100 ASEAN projects last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have supported our companies to capture these opportunities by catalysing capability development, market access and access to manpower and financing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will continue to facilitate our companies’ foray overseas through our network of overseas centres, which supported over 100 projects in ASEAN last year.

sections.label: GRTP programme components
sections.summary: The GRTP has overseas internships for Singapore students and a management associate programme, with up to 70% funding for participant allowance or salary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The GRTP comprises two components – overseas internships for Singapore students, and a management associate programme for young professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore enterprises can receive up to 70% funding support for the allowance or salary of participants.

sections.label: EDG and PSG support extension
sections.summary: Enhanced 70% support under EDG and PSG is extended another three years, till the end of FY2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, we will extend the enhanced 70% support under EDG for another three years, till the end of financial year (FY) 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, we will extend the enhanced support of up to 70% under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) for another three years as well, till the end of FY2022.

sections.label: Sectoral approach via ITMs
sections.summary: In the first phase, a sectoral approach was taken through the 23 launched ITMs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the first phase, we have taken a sectoral approach through the 23 ITMs that have been launched.

sections.label: SATS-BRF Food productivity gains
sections.summary: SATS-BRF Food improved meat-cutting productivity, achieving 18% manpower savings and freeing workers for new business initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: One beneficiary of this programme is SATS-BRF Food, a food processing and distribution company.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It has improved the productivity of its core meat-cutting operations, achieving 18% manpower savings and freeing up workers to support new business initiatives.

sections.label: Funded assessments for manufacturing
sections.summary: Over 230 funded assessments have been awarded, helping more than 150 manufacturing companies prepare for Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To date, we have awarded over 230 funded assessments and helped more than 150 manufacturing companies better prepare for Industry 4.0.

sections.label: Manufacturing event Singapore edition
sections.summary: A platform for manufacturers, technology providers and thought leaders drew 15,000 visitors from 55 countries, exceeding the goal by 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It is a platform for leading manufacturers, technology providers and thought leaders to exchange ideas and best practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This Singapore edition attracted 15,000 visitors across 55 countries, exceeding our initial goal by 50%.

sections.label: Agri-Food Innovation Park Sungei Kadut
sections.summary: An 18-hectare Agri-Food Innovation Park in Sungei Kadut will host high-tech farming and R&D, ready from Q2 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To catalyse agri-tech innovation and co-creation among industry players, we need to strengthen our infrastructure support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: So, I am pleased to announce that we will establish a new 18-hectare Agri-Food Innovation Park (AFIP) in Sungei Kadut.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: AFIP will bring together high-tech farming and R&D activities, including indoor plant factories, insect farms, and animal feed production facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We are working with local and overseas industry players to develop this first phase of the park, which will be ready from the second quarter of 2021, with potential for future expansion, depending on demand.

sections.label: Temasek Polytechnic Aquaculture Innovation Centre
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat said in his Budget speech that Temasek Polytechnic will launch a Centre of Innovation in Aquaculture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat also mentioned in his Budget speech that Temasek Polytechnic will be launching a Centre of Innovation in Aquaculture.

sections.label: EDG funding and IGP merger
sections.summary: EDG funding support is extended three years at up to 70% of qualifying costs, and IGP merges into EDG with worker outcome commitments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As Minister Chan Chun Sing mentioned, the EDG's enhanced funding support will be extended for three more years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Companies will enjoy up to 70% of qualifying costs till end of FY 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will merge IGP into the EDG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Liang Eng Hwa will be pleased to note that through this merger, we will encourage companies to more intentionally translate enterprise transformation efforts into improvements in workers' livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will do so by requiring businesses embarking on EDG projects from 1 April 2020 to commit to the fulfillment of workers' outcomes.

sections.label: PSG training subsidy
sections.summary: Enterprises qualifying for PSG can apply for a training subsidy covering 70% of out-of-pocket training expenses, capped at $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Enterprises which qualify for PSG can apply for a training subsidy to cover 70% of their out-of-pocket training expenses, capped at $10,000 per enterprise.

sections.label: Research agencies industry collaboration
sections.summary: Research agencies are encouraged to collaborate with industry so companies benefit from R&D and commercialise IP, with over 1,500 industry projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We encourage our research agencies to collaborate with industry players so that companies can benefit from the R&D and commercialise the IP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: There are more than 1,500 industry projects deploying more than 1,000 technologies developed by our researchers.

sections.label: Singapore businesses overseas activities survey
sections.summary: In 2018, seven in 10 Singapore businesses surveyed by SBF had activities in overseas markets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2018, seven in 10 Singapore businesses surveyed by SBF have activities in overseas markets.

sections.label: ESG internationalisation projects 2018
sections.summary: ESG supported over 570 internationalisation-related projects in 2018, a 25% increase from 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To Mr Henry Kwek's query, ESG supported over 570 internationalisation-related projects in 2018, a 25% increase compared to 2017.

sections.label: EFS overseas financing support changes
sections.summary: The Government will raise EFS overseas project financing insurance cover to $50 million and tenure to 15 years, with higher M&A loan cover and risk share for young enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government will raise the maximum insurance cover for overseas project financing under EFS to $50 million and increase the maximum tenure to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To support companies that are internationalising via mergers and acquisitions (M&A), the scheme will provide a higher maximum loan cover of $50 million for such projects to allow companies to quickly build new capabilities and expand overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government will support a higher risk share for loans to young enterprises under EFS, for both domestic and international projects.

sections.label: ESG collaborative initiatives and overseas projects
sections.summary: Last year, ESG facilitated over 30 collaborative initiatives and supported over 40 companies to win new overseas projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Last year, ESG facilitated over 30 collaborative initiatives and supported over 40 companies to win new projects in overseas markets.

sections.label: LEAD programme support since 2005
sections.summary: Since its 2005 launch, the LEAD programme has supported more than 50 TACs in projects involving close to 52,000 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2005, the LEAD programme has supported more than 50 TACs in spearheading projects involving close to 52,000 companies.

sections.label: SMECEN manhour savings and funding
sections.summary: SMEs adopting SMECEN can cut average manhours per job by up to 80%, and maximum funding rose from 70% to 90% for high-impact multi-TAC projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: SMEs adopting SMECEN can reduce the average manhours per job by up to 80%, which will allow their workers to take on higher-value work, higher-value functions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: The maximum funding level was also increased from 70% to 90% of qualifying costs for high-impact projects involving multiple TACs.

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Panel licensing best practices
sections.summary: The Pro-Enterprise Panel and agencies developed licensing best practices and reviewed over 1,000 regulations since 2000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: To Mr Lee Yi Shyan's query, the Pro-Enterprise Panel (PEP) and agencies have, together, developed the best practices on licensing approaches.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: They have also reviewed and streamlined more than 1,000 regulations since PEP’s formation in 2000, based on ground feedback and international reports on the ease of doing business in Singapore.

sections.label: Red Dot Power exit
sections.summary: Red Dot Power mainly retailed to businesses, was not in the full OEM launch, and exited due to cash flow issues.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: Red Dot Power was predominantly retailing to businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: It was not involved in the full OEM launch and we understand that Red Dot Power's exit was due to cash flow issues.

sections.label: Inhouse credit sales agreements regulation
sections.summary: Retailers offering inhouse credit sales agreements are not specifically regulated but remain subject to general laws like the Sale of Goods Act and CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: While retailers offering inhouse credit sales agreements are not specifically regulated today, they are still subject to general laws, like the Sale of Goods Act and CPFTA.

sections.label: Review of industry practices
sections.summary: The Government is working with stakeholders to review industry practices and the appropriate regulatory response.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: The Government is working with stakeholders to review industry practices and the appropriate regulatory response.

sections.label: MAS study of chargeback policies
sections.summary: MAS will study Mr Lim Biow Chuan's suggestion to reference the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's approach to chargeback policies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
sentences.text: On Mr Lim Biow Chuan's suggestion for MAS to take reference from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's approach to chargeback policies, MAS will study this.

sections.label: RCEP conclusion determination
sections.summary: RCEP Ministerial colleagues reaffirmed their determination to try their best to conclude RCEP this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What I sense from my RCEP Ministerial colleagues is that all of them have reaffirmed their determination to try their best to conclude RCEP this year.

sections.label: Ministers agree 2019 workplan
sections.summary: Ministers agreed on a 2019 workplan with monthly intermediate targets to reach the finishing line by year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Over the weekend, the Ministers have agreed on a 2019 workplan which will include intermediate targets to be achieved each month for us to ensure that we get to the finishing line by the end of this year.

sections.label: Four regional elections
sections.summary: There are four regional elections: India, Indonesia, Thailand and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In particular, there are four regional elections: India, Indonesia, Thailand and Australia.

sections.label: Next Ministerial meeting milestone
sections.summary: The next critical milestone for the Ministerial meeting will be in August this year in China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The next critical milestone for the Ministerial meeting will be in August this year in China.

sections.label: Defence industry and economy
sections.summary: The defence industry can contribute to the overall economy, with almost half of ST Engineering's business from the non-defence sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Whether we see the defence industry as able to contribute to our overall economy, the answer is definitely yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In fact, if you look at ST Engineering today, I do not have the exact numbers, but if I am not wrong, almost half of their business comes from the non-defence sector.

sections.label: Malaysia in ASEAN economy
sections.summary: Malaysia is part of the wider ASEAN economy, and uncertainties in its economy will affect Singapore and regional countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, is that Malaysia is part of the wider ASEAN economy and, obviously, any uncertainties in Malaysia's economy will affect Singapore, just as it will affect the regional countries.

sections.label: Malaysia disruption impacts Singapore
sections.summary: Disruption to the Malaysian economy will significantly impact Singapore's economy, so MTI has encouraged companies to consider Malaysia's trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Having said that, of course, any disruption to the Malaysian economy can have and will have a significant impact on Singapore's economy, which is why, over the last few months, MTI has been encouraging our companies to seriously consider the impact of Malaysia’s political and economic trajectory.
